title: Data plane: propagate burst admission headers/claims into routing + logging context
author: Emily Zhao
description:
Context: Burst capacity (Dedicated) introduces an admission decision that happens before routing selects a backend pool. We need end-to-end traceability for: (a) why a request was routed to baseline vs burst, (b) why burst was denied (limit, cooldown, saturation gate), and (c) which burst pool was used when admitted. Today, the policy engine returns an admission decision to the edge, but the router and downstream logs only see “baseline vs not baseline” implicitly.

This PR wires burst admission information through the data-plane request path by propagating a small, explicitly allow-listed set of internal headers and mapping them into the routing context + structured logs + trace baggage. This is intentionally not a metrics PR (ENG-4826 covers counters/labels); the goal here is making single-request debugging and post-incident forensics possible without requiring log joins across services.

What’s in this change: (1) Define internal header contract for burst admission: x-rw-burst-requested, x-rw-burst-decision, x-rw-burst-pool, x-rw-burst-deny-reason, x-rw-burst-policy-rev, x-rw-burst-claim (signed opaque token for internal use). (2) Edge/gateway: propagate the above headers from the policy evaluation result to the internal request forwarded to router. If headers are missing or invalid, we default to baseline behavior and set decision=not_evaluated for logging. (3) Router: parse and validate the headers (strict allow-list, bounded sizes), attach a BurstAdmission object to the request context, and expose normalized fields to route selection + logs/traces. (4) Logging: add structured fields (burst.requested, burst.decision, burst.pool, burst.deny_reason, burst.policy_rev) to router access logs and scheduler handoff logs. Deny reason is normalized to a small enum to avoid leaking internals / high-cardinality strings. (5) Tracing: add burst fields to trace baggage for the router span only (NOT emitted to customer responses). (6) Safety: strip any inbound x-rw-burst-* headers from external requests at the edge; only internal trusted components can set these.

Notes/decisions: - Header naming intentionally uses x-rw-* to avoid collisions and to make it easy to filter/strip at the edge. - The x-rw-burst-claim is treated as opaque here; this PR only transports it and enforces max length. Verification/signing enforcement remains in the policy service + router follow-up (tracked in ENG-4833 security review). - We do not surface these headers to customers in responses. This PR only affects internal hops and internal logging.

Testing: unit tests for header parsing/normalization, fuzz-ish tests for oversized headers, and an integration test that exercises baseline -> burst-admitted path and verifies the router emits the expected structured log fields.

Rollout plan: safe to deploy behind the existing burst feature flag. When burst is disabled, no headers are produced and the parser yields decision=not_requested; logs should remain stable.

Follow-ups: - Metrics emission keyed off these normalized fields (ENG-4826). - Audit log linkage of policy_rev/claim id (ENG-4833). - Docs for oncall: how to grep logs using burst.deny_reason and burst.policy_rev (runbook update).
commits: dataplane/gateway: strip external x-rw-burst-* headers; propagate internal burst headers to router hop
router: parse burst admission headers into RequestContext::BurstAdmission (normalized enum + pool id)
logging: add burst.* structured fields to router access logs + scheduler handoff logs
tracing: attach burst decision + pool to router span baggage (internal only)
tests: header parsing validation + integration coverage for admitted/denied paths
chore: update internal header allow-list documentation

services/router/src/routing/route_selector.rs (plumb BurstAdmission into routing context; no behavior change beyond observability)

review_conversation: Ravi Menon: Can we guarantee we don’t ever trust x-rw-burst-* from the public internet? We’ve had issues with “internal header” assumptions before. Emily Zhao: Yep — gateway now strips any inbound x-rw-burst-* on external listeners. Only the internal policy->gateway path can set them. Added a regression test in header_sanitizer.rs.

Mina Haddad: Does adding these headers change routing behavior in any way? I want to avoid subtle baseline vs burst selection changes sneaking in. Emily Zhao: No functional routing change in this PR. The router attaches BurstAdmission to context for observability and future routing use, but route_selector only reads it to annotate the chosen route; it doesn’t alter pool selection logic here.

Jordan Lee: Deny reason strings coming from policy can get verbose (and potentially high-cardinality). Please normalize to an enum before logging. Emily Zhao: Done. Added BurstDenyReason enum with small set: LIMIT_TPS, LIMIT_CONCURRENCY, COOLDOWN, SATURATION_GATE, NOT_ELIGIBLE, INVALID_CLAIM, UNKNOWN. Parser maps anything else to UNKNOWN.

Logan Wright: Please keep pool identifiers stable and low-cardinality; avoid logging raw instance IDs. Are we logging pool name or pool UUID? Emily Zhao: Logging uses pool_id (region/gpu-type pool key, e.g., us-east-1/h100/burst-a). No instance IDs. Also added max length checks and truncation to avoid log abuse.

Peter Holtz: Trace baggage can blow up spans if we add too many keys. Can we keep it to decision + pool only, and ensure bounded sizes? Emily Zhao: Updated. Only two baggage keys: burst.decision and burst.pool, both bounded to 64 chars. deny_reason stays in logs only.

Vikram Singh: Looks good. One nit: the header parser returns not_evaluated when headers are missing, but the description says not_requested. Can we align names? Emily Zhao: Aligned to not_requested for the “burst wasn’t asked for” case and not_evaluated only when requested=true but decision header missing/invalid. Updated tests accordingly.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash on 2025-07-11 after approvals from Mina Haddad and Ravi Menon; CI green.
